summary.headline: Newgen Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR357 crore and PAT 26% to INR63 crore, with annuity revenue up 14% to INR254 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR357 crore, up 11% YoY, led by annuity revenue of about INR254 crore (up 14%) and SaaS/subscription revenue of about INR60 crore (up 40%). Implementation revenue declined sharply on project start delays, mainly in EMEA and India, which management expects to recover in Q2 and Q3. EBITDA adjusted for other income was INR56 crore (15.7% margin) and PAT was INR63 crore (17.6% net margin), with management reiterating expected full-year margin expansion. Leadership changed: Tarun Nandwani becomes CEO from 1 August 2026, and a Chief Growth Officer role was created.

segments.name: EMEA
segments.commentary: Largest region at about INR114 crore, growing 10% YoY; implementation starts were delayed, and macro conditions delayed some payments.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: About INR96 crore in revenue; management said India did not grow and base costs rose 4-5%, squeezing India margin. Pipeline reported as growing on NBFC LOS/LMS and trade deals.

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: About INR92 crore, up 27% YoY, the fastest-growing region, on subscription model; management said some large deals were in the INR12-16 crore range.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: About INR56 crore, growing 12% YoY; government knowledge management and LOS/LMS seeing traction.

segments.name: Verticals
segments.commentary: Banking and financial services about INR225 crore, growing 5%; insurance and healthcare about INR79 crore, growing 58%. Management named banking, insurance, healthcare and government as focus areas; the remaining verticals were not quantified.

guidance_outlook: Management expects full-year EBITDA margin expansion, with annual margins typically 23-25% on a different basis; Q1 is the seasonally lowest margin quarter. Analyst-cited 15-16% range was not confirmed by management.
Management said it will maintain a 20% margin level as its target, which was not clearly reconciled with the 15.7% Q1 margin.
Expects implementation revenue to recover roughly INR12 crore lost in Q1 during Q2 and Q3 as projects kicked off.
No formal revenue guidance; management hopes to maintain double-digit growth in coming quarters.
Expects India and EMEA to return to growth; DSO expected to decline in coming quarters.
Buyback proposal has been given to the Board; acquisitions still under evaluation; dividend to be increased each year.
capex_capacity: Headcount about 4,200 at end FY26 and currently at a similar level, flat versus prior year; management attributed efficiency to AI-led engineering gains.
No capex or capacity figures were disclosed on the call.
demand_pricing: Added 10 new logos in Q1; four large deals disclosed: Kuwait core insurance policy administration INR26.7 crore, Philippines retail loan origination INR16.2 crore, Annapurna Finance AI-enabled LOS/collection INR15.6 crore, UK ECM INR14.5 crore.
Booking growth reported as double digit for the year; bookings and pipeline to be disclosed annually in March. Management declined to provide RPO data.
AI-led vertical products (trade finance, insurance, healthcare, government) sold as part of vertical product offerings; pricing model evolving and not yet settled.
DSO elevated in Q1 versus prior periods but improved from Q4 to Q1, per management.
Licence revenue concentrated in India and EMEA; mature markets are mostly subscription-based.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion and is 15-16% sustainable for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarun Nandwani attributed margin gains to AI optimisation in engineering and said efficiency gains are passed on to customers; management said full-year EBITDA margin should expand and Q1 is the seasonal low.

qa_highlights.question: Why did implementation revenue fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays in project starts due to customer environmental factors, specifically India and EMEA, after a weak licence year; management expects recovery in Q2 from existing executed order book.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a headcount reduction and where?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount was about 4,200 at end FY26 and is flat now; efficiencies said to be broad-based across products, accelerators and delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Will Newgen disclose RPO data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said subscription revenue is only about 12-13% of total and RPO is not disclosed; they may share more in future but bookings growth is the current parameter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income elevated and why did the other vertical slow?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income reflects treasury income plus mark-to-market gains on treasury and currency; Q1 is seasonally heavier. Management said the focus verticals are banking, insurance, healthcare and government, with other verticals covering 14-15 sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Any acquisitions or buyback plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition is under deliberation for a couple of years with no fit yet; buyback proposal has been given to the Board.

risks_watch: Implementation revenue decline and project start delays in EMEA and India; recovery of about INR12 crore needed in Q2-Q3.
India margin pressure: flat top line and base costs up 4-5%.
DSO elevated and EMEA payment delays from macro conditions.
Leadership transition: CEO change effective 1 August 2026.
Headcount flat at about 4,200 while licence and implementation revenue are weak; watch delivery capacity.
Non-disclosure of RPO and quarterly bookings limits visibility into SaaS momentum.
summary.management_tone: Confident on annuity growth and margins but cautious and somewhat evasive on quarterly guidance, implementation timing and India/EMEA recovery, repeatedly deferring to full-year numbers.
key_quotes: We have started FY '27 on a steady note with Q1 reflecting continued resilience in our business model, sustained customer engagement and healthy momentum to our annuity-led revenue streams.
So we are expecting India and EMEA to come back to growth numbers.
But it is being a first quarter, obviously, it is not appropriate to comment beyond this as far as the overall number is concerned.

financial_highlights.change: Margin up from about 14% as cited by an analyst

financial_highlights.value: Down about 23% YoY, about INR12 crore shortfall per management
financial_highlights.change: Down YoY, figure as stated by management

growth.why: Management hopes to maintain double-digit revenue growth (held guidance, no formal number) and expects about INR12 crore of lost implementation revenue to recover in Q2-Q3, with Q1 revenue up 11% and annuity up 14%; backing is demand and pipeline commentary with no capacity, and the 10 logos and four large deals are only partial support.

roles: Chief Executive Officer (Tarun Nandwani, effective 1 August 2026)
mgmt.note: Tarun Nandwani becomes CEO from 1 August 2026 and a Chief Growth Officer role was created; no specific growth plan or targets were detailed on the call.
